Earlier gameplay summary (agent-written, uncertain claims remain uncertain):
CONTROLS: Left/Right=move, Z=jump (0.8s reaches elevated platforms, 0.7s tested), X=attack, Down=crouch (tested, no visible effect at shell area), Up+X=upward attack, Down+X=downward attack, Left+C or Right+C=dash, A=bind (9+ tests no effect), Escape=pause. Character: masked figure white horned mask, red cloak, nail weapon. Health: 6 masks.

SAVE: 1h31m playtime, Moss Grotto, 1% completion, 0 currency. Version 1.0.30000.

MAP DISCOVERED: Started in horizontal cave system with two vertical levels. LOWER LEVEL: Stone well left ~(0.12,0.45) non-interactive, ornate SPHERE center-right ~(0.68-0.70,0.50-0.55) bronze/gold carved - tested 10+ times all methods no effect, character passes through. UPPER LEVEL: Accessed via 0.8s Left+Z jump. Spiral SHELL/FOSSIL structure ~(0.62-0.65,0.48) on upper level - tested X, A no effect.

MAJOR PROGRESSION: Left+Z jump at ~(0.52,0.68) from blocked left boundary triggered ZONE TRANSITION through dark passage in left wall into NEW FOREST ZONE with darker teal-blue atmosphere, massive twisted organic root/branch archways creating tunnel passages, different from starting cave. Explored new zone - path loops back to massive ornate SPIRAL SHELL/CAGE structure (same or similar to earlier shell) from different angles.

CURRENT AREA: Stone cobblestone path level with massive ornate bronze spiral shell structure. Shell displays intricate bronze/gold carved patterns with leaf/vine/organic swirl designs, small decorative spiral element protrudes from top. Shell confirmed NON-INTERACTIVE - tested X attack on shell body and bronze lever/handle at base ~(0.48-0.49,0.73-0.75) all no effect, pure background decoration. Character can walk past/through shell - it renders as background element. RIGHT of shell: dead-end mossy rock wall with mushrooms confirmed. LEFT of shell: stone path continues with black mushroom silhouettes (flat caps and tall stems throughout).

LAST ACTION: 0.7s Right+Z jump from ~(0.55,0.72) toward mushroom caps at ~(0.66,0.68) and ~(0.80,0.74) - testing if mushroom caps are solid platforms, bounce surfaces, or provide elevation access (inspired by H-K style mechanics possibility).

COMBAT: X=one-hit kill on bugs. Four enemies defeated in starting area, auto-collect currency. No respawns observed. No enemies encountered in new forest zone yet.

FAILED STRATEGIES: Sphere/shell interaction all methods (10+ tests on original sphere, X attack on current shell and bronze lever), A key 9+ locations, Down key at shell area (no crouch/drop), 0.8s jump from shell left side did not clear shell height, attacking mushrooms/walls, solo C key, waiting, extended boundary testing.

ENVIRONMENT FEATURES: Elaborate hanging moss formations, black mushroom silhouettes (flat caps low ~0.79 and tall stems throughout), green glowing particles ambient, dramatic cyan-teal pillar/beam structures observed in darker sections suggesting architectural elements, massive black ceiling mass with hanging spike at ~(0.40,0.45) in current view.

ACTIVE GOAL: Find progression route beyond shell area. 1% completion indicates vast unexplored content. Current hypothesis: mushroom caps may be solid platforms or bounce surfaces for vertical access (untested). Stone cobblestone path suggests structured route to important location. Darker atmospheric sections with architectural pillar structures may indicate shrine/boss/significant areas not yet accessed.

UNRESOLVED: A (bind) function 9+ tests no effect. Solo C function no effect. Multiple shell/sphere structures purpose unknown despite prominent placement. Health upgrade from 5 to 6 masks mechanism unknown (occurred between sessions). Mushroom interaction mechanics unknown - flat caps and tall stems untested as jump platforms. Stone path destination unknown. Architectural pillar/beam structures in darker sections not yet investigated closely. Progression route location - extensive two-level starting cave and new forest zone explored, shell area appears bounded but vertical/bounce mechanics not fully tested.
